text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Banco Totta e Acores has reference value of 3,000 escudos per share, according to a source close to the bank's board. The valuation was delivered to Under Secretary for Finance Fernando Teixeira Santos last Friday. The governnment plans to sell a 13.22 percent stake in the bank later this year.
- Centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) is to decide next Tuesday whether to join the European Popular Party.
- Detailed bills will be available to all Portugal Telecom customers from March.
- A threatened strike by drivers of milk company Agros on November 4 and 5 could jeopardise the collection of two million litres of milk.
- Soccer club Benfica technicaly bankrupt, according to an audit carried out by Arthur Andersen.
- Sonangalp, a joint venture between Angolan oil company Sonangol and Portuguese oil company Petrogal, plans to open eight petrol stations in Angola for a 1.5 billion escudos investment.
- The selection jury favours U.S. company Philip Morris in the public competition to buy state owned tobacco company Tabaqueira, the paper learned. The government has yet to take a final decision.

- Crisis-torn rightwing Popular Party (PP) has seen its support plunge to three percent of voters from nine percent over the past month, although sympathy for the PP's embattled leader Manuel Monteiro has risen sharply, according to an opinion poll.
- Around 3,000 civil servants protested yesterday against the government's 1997 wage proposals.
